item.title: AI Is Changing the Security Game. That’s Why My Jump Host Strategy Matters More Than Ever.
item.description:
AI Is Changing the Security Game. That’s Why My Jump Host Strategy Matters More Than Ever.

October 21, 2026 · Security · Homelab · Infrastructure

The day the PHP vulnerability became a wake-up call

Today’s critical PHP security release is a reminder of how quickly the security landscape is changing.

Two critical vulnerabilities, rated CVSS 9.2, have been fixed in PHP. Under certain conditions, they allow unauthenticated remote code execution — potentially giving an attacker the ability to execute code on a vulnerable server without first logging in.

item.title: From Raspberry Pi to Mac: Simplifying My Amiga Setup with AmiKit X13.1
item.description:
JIT compilation support has been available in Amiberry since version 8.0.0, but I started my macOS setup with Amiberry 8.3.0 on an Apple Silicon Mac mini with an M2 chip. This combination made me reconsider my existing Amiga setup.

Originally, I deliberately kept AmiKit X13.1 on a dedicated Raspberry Pi. I liked having a separate machine for retro computing, independent of my everyday environment. It was a perfectly reasonable setup, and the Raspberry Pi could always find another purpose down the road.

item.title: Joule vs. Copilot: What’s the Difference?
item.description:
Joule vs. GitHub Copilot: Where I See the Difference

After working with both SAP Joule for Developers and GitHub Copilot in an ABAP development environment, I currently see a fairly clear distinction between the two.

Joule feels like a very capable SAP-native development assistant. It understands the SAP context well and is particularly useful for things like explaining ABAP code, generating tests, and working with SAP-specific tools such as RAP generators or Custom Fields and Logic.

item.title: Safari 27, a Ghost Miro Popup, and the Most Expensive Bookmark I've Ever Debugged
item.description:
A Safari 27 debugging story featuring LaunchServices, SQLite, binary plists, and a single corrupted bookmark.

For the next poor soul (or AI agent) who lands here after Googling “Safari miroapp popup at startup”, here’s what happened.

The symptom

Every time Safari started, about 10 seconds later I got a popup asking to open Miro.

The URL was always identical:

miroapp://miro.com/app/board/<my_blog_identifier>/

The funny part? Miro wasn’t installed.

What we ruled out

Naturally, we started with the obvious.
